dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: The strongest warriors of all have to be the two Masters-tier warriors...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Strongest warriors"?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you, Honorary Knight. I am categorizing the opponents we've encountered on our expeditions so far into five tiers based on their combat strength.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: The tiers, from the least powerful to the most, are: Pre-Captains, Captains, Super Captains, Pre-Masters, and Masters.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it then.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: I need to keep improving...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you not have a tier that's even higher than that?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Ahem, in that case, we would be talking about the ones with weird powers, like gods, demons and ancient dragons...!

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: I'm not really creating a power ranking. The whole point of this exercise is to help me establish my standards and set a goal for myself. So why would I include all that?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Besides, there are so many factors that go into a loss or a victory. Things like the strengths and weaknesses of each side, and the proper application of battle tactics, these are all important... Only people who don't understand battle come up with those silly rankings and lists all the time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, who do you have in the Masters tier?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Our very own Grand Master Varka's one of 'em, for sure! As for others...

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: In all our time during the expedition to Nod-Krai, the only other one we've met who can compare is the head of the Fatui Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: But annoyingly, he's also referred to as "The Captain," which makes discussions about battle power quite confusing, especially with the Captains tier! Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So which tier do I fall into?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Uh... Huh? Um...

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: You know, I haven't really thought about that before... I'm sorry. Maybe because our Honorary Knight over here is so lowkey most of the time.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: #If I really have to... I feel like I should start a "{NICKNAME} tier" just for you alone?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You... are right.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: ...But come to think of it, Teyvat is a huge place, and it's been said that there has been a human warrior who managed to ascend to the divine throne.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Too bad the Grand Master didn't bring me along when he went to Natlan... Otherwise, who knows? I might have found a really solid candidate for the "Super Masters" tier!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could use this ranking as a guide when facing enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: That is true... You know what? I'll come up with a "Hypothetical Opponent Ranking" when I have the time.

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: No matter how I look at it, the Lupus Boreas and Decarabian would belong in the "Super Gods and Demons" tier... In that case, wouldn't Rächer of Solnari be in the "Ultra Gods and Demons" tier?

dialogues.speaker: Leifhelm
dialogues.text: Oh, I should mention — we've had quite a few signs of wolf activity around here lately. Since they tell me you're a pretty famous Adventurer, Honorary Knight, I figured you'd be interested in knowing that?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Turn, left... turn, right!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Honorary Knight, feel like helping me get them cleaned up?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Oh, just some Knights of Favonius formation drills. These three overdid it last night, so I'm sobering them up.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...And rooting out the worst offender while I'm at it, whose grand prize will be 20 laps. The expeditionary force is allowed to drink liquor, but ground rules stand for when and how much you drink.

response.speaker: Winfried
response.text: I—I only had a little bit!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Save the excuses, prove it with your feet! Show me you can nail a picture-perfect parade-ground pivot while you're plastered!
